input.brief: Data analyst in NT Government (Darwin) applying for reporting and analytics roles; evidence-based reporting, Power BI dashboards, data pipelines, plain-English insight for non-technical audiences

direction.name: The split stage
direction.idea: Half the screen never moves. One side is a fixed photograph (or object, or product view) that stays in place for the whole visit; the other side is a calm scrolling column with everything you need to read. The fixed half keeps the feeling present while the reader gets on with the facts, like sitting in the room while reading the menu. As sections pass, the fixed image may quietly change to the one that matches.
direction.composition: Desktop: a two-column page, 50/50 or 45/55. One column is `position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh` and holds a single photograph filling it edge to edge, or the object centred on a flat field. The other column scrolls and holds all content in a single narrow measure (max 46ch) with comfortable padding (48–72px): name and one-line description first, then sections separated by generous space, then contact and footer. Headings in the scrolling column are modest (32–44px). The column grounds differ: photograph on one side, flat paper colour on the other, meeting at a clean vertical edge. On a phone the fixed half becomes a 60svh image at the top that stays sticky behind the first section, then releases.
direction.typography: A text-first setting: a readable serif or a calm sans at 17–19px, with one display size for the name. Left-aligned throughout.
direction.colour: The paper colour of the reading column is chosen against the photograph: a tone taken from its shadows or its lightest area. One ink, optionally one accent ink for links and the action.
direction.imagery: One excellent portrait-orientation photograph for the fixed half, plus three or four more that crossfade in as their sections arrive. Small inline photographs in the reading column are optional and should be few.
direction.richness: A full-height photograph always in view, against a quiet, well-set column of text.
direction.pitfalls: The reading column must be genuinely well typeset, since it is half the page. Do not put cards or grids in it. Check that the fixed image crops well at short viewport heights. In blind tests the commonest complaint was monotony: several screens of the same split with only the text changing. Change what the reading half holds from section to section (a list, a large figure, a table, a full-colour panel, a drawing) and let at least one section break the split and run full width.

hero.name: Striped card beside the room
hero.blueprint: The viewport is split 50/50 with a 12px gap and 12px outer margins. The right half is one full-height photograph of the room, corners radiused 16px, `position: sticky` so it stays in view while the left half scrolls. The left half is a printed card: a flat paper-colour panel with the same 16px radius, and the subject's stripe (from its awning, label or ribbon) as the only ornament. Across the card's top runs a band 56px tall made of alternating bars of the single ink colour and paper, each bar 28px wide, built as a flex row of filled blocks. The same stripe returns as an 8px band above the footer and inside the button on hover. Under the band, centred: the wordmark about 300px wide, then a two-line headline in a light serif at clamp(40px, 3.6vw, 56px) in the ink colour, one supporting sentence at 17px held to 36ch, and the single action as a solid rectangular button. Three text links sit in one centred row at 15px, 28px above the card's bottom edge. One ink on paper; the photograph supplies every other colour.
hero.mobile: The photograph comes first at full width inside 12px margins, 48svh tall, with the 16px radius. The card follows and overlaps the photograph's bottom edge by 24px using a negative margin. Its striped band is 40px tall; below it the wordmark at 56% width, the headline at 8vw on two lines, the sentence and the button, all centred. The links wrap into the card's foot.
hero.headline: A warm two-line welcome of three to six words, up to about 18 characters per line at 3.6vw.

type.note: The plain Times-style roman of a typed document, slightly tightened and never larger than a few vw. Suits vehicles and tools presented dryly, artists' pages, investment memos and anything meant to look undesigned on purpose.

palette.name: Charcoal and sage
palette.note: Charcoal holds the page with off-white text, and one section may flip to a pale concrete tone with dark text. Colour comes from the photographs; grey sage is used for the single button and the active state of a control.

motion.name: Slow crossfade
motion.description: The principal photograph quietly changes: three or four images of the same framing crossfade over about 1.6 seconds, holding five to six seconds each, or the fixed image changes when its matching section arrives. It should feel like light shifting in a room. Pause when the tab is hidden; under reduced motion show only the first image.

sections.name: Title torn at the seam
sections.blueprint: A wrapper about 95svh tall per project holds a sticky stage of 100svh, split at exactly 50vw into two portrait panes of 720×900px, `object-fit: cover`, square corners, no gap: two different pictures or loops of the same project (the whole and a detail, before and after). The project's title sits on the seam, centred on x 720 at the optical middle: capitals in a heavy face at clamp(96px, 11vw, 160px), leading 0.8, tracking -0.04em, at most two lines, in one light colour chosen per project. It is set twice inside the one heading element, the second copy `aria-hidden`, each copy clipped to its own half with `clip-path: inset(0 50% 0 0)` and `inset(0 0 0 50%)`. Directly under it, centred, the discipline and year at 16px and a text link with an arrow at 16px. While a project crosses the stage, the left pane and left half-title travel up and the right pane and right half-title travel down (panes ±20svh, title ±30svh, on a scroll-linked timeline), so the name tears at the seam and lines up exactly when the project is centred. The section's two-word heading sits at clamp(28px, 2.4vw, 36px) in the stage's top-left corner, 32px in. Four to eight projects; the stage releases after the last. Under reduced motion the halves stay aligned and the projects change by crossfade.
sections.mobile: Keep the split: two strips 195px wide running the full height of the screen with the same opposing travel. The title drops to 12.5vw on the seam, at most two lines, with the discipline line and the link under it at 16px; give the link a 44px hit area.

sections.name: Sticky photograph, active list
sections.blueprint: Two columns. The left, columns 1–5, is `position: sticky; top: 12vh` and holds one photograph or object at 4:5, 34vw wide, unframed on the ground. The right, columns 7–11, holds a vertical list of five to nine names (treatments, rooms, courses, services) at clamp(20px, 1.6vw, 24px), each row 58px tall with the name at the left and a price or duration right-aligned at 15px in the soft ink. The active row is full ink; the others rest at 40% opacity. Hovering, focusing or scrolling a row to the middle of the viewport makes it active, crossfades the left photograph to that item's image over 300ms, and opens a three-line description at 15px, 34ch wide, directly under the name, pushing later rows down. A heading of two or three words at clamp(32px, 3.4vw, 48px) sits above the list, aligned to its left edge, 48px above the first row.
sections.mobile: The photograph becomes a 4:3 band pinned to the top of the screen at 38svh while the list scrolls beneath it; the heading sits above the first row. Rows are 56px tall and the description opens on tap. The image changes with the row nearest the band.

sections.name: Output index, live sheet
sections.blueprint: For products that make documents: invoices, reports, emails, statements. Columns 1–5 list the names of three to five outputs, one per line, at clamp(36px, 4vw, 64px), leading 1.1, each a `<button>`; the selected name is in full ink, the rest in the soft ink. There is no other heading. Columns 7–12 are a stage in a flat tone one step from the ground, 88svh tall, and on it lies the selected output as an object: a paper-white sheet 560px wide, built in HTML at true size, root marked data-ui, with a real sender, real line items, sums that add up and a date. The sheet starts 72px below the stage's top and runs past its bottom edge, which crops it. Selecting a name swaps the sheet with a 200ms crossfade; an email is narrower (440px), a receipt narrower still (300px), all left-aligned 64px into the stage.
sections.mobile: Names become one sideways-scrolling row at 22px with scroll-snap, the selected one in full ink. Beneath, the stage fills the width and is 70svh tall; the sheet keeps its true size, anchored top-left with a 16px inset and cropped by the stage's right and bottom edges. Tapping a name swaps it.

sections.name: Plain names in columns
sections.blueprint: A typographic list with no logos. The heading, two or three words at 28–32px, sits in columns 1–3 and stays top-aligned with the first row of names. Columns 5–12 hold the names in three or four text columns (`columns: 4; column-gap: 32px`), each name on its own line at 20–22px with leading 1.5, sentence case, in the full ink. Where names fall into kinds (clients, press, partners), each kind starts a new column and its first line names the kind in the softer ink at the same size, so no small labels are needed. Columns are of unequal length and are not balanced; ragged bottoms are intended. Twelve to thirty names work best. There are no boxes, bullets or separators: the column edges and the shared baseline do the organising. Leave 120px above and below.
sections.mobile: The heading leads at 26px. Names follow in two columns at 17px with a 20px gap; each kind begins after a 32px break with its name in the softer ink on the first line. Long names wrap inside their column rather than shrinking.

sections.name: Founder's letter
sections.blueprint: A letter in a centred column 520px wide with at least 160px of empty ground above and below. At the column's top-left, a round portrait 44px across. 28px below it, four or five short paragraphs at 16–17px with leading 1.55, each two to four lines and separated by one blank line, written in the first person. No heading. The sign-off is the writer's name at 22px in the text face's italic, with the role at 14px in the soft ink beneath it. One phrase in the letter may carry a flat marker-colour background. Variant for a page built as an object: the letter sits on a filled paper-colour sheet 640px wide with 60px padding on a contrasting ground, square corners, its bottom edge cut into small scallops with `clip-path`, and below a row of 5px round dots a tear-off strip 72px tall that carries the email address.
sections.mobile: The column takes the full width with 24px margins; text at 16px, portrait 40px. In the sheet variant the sheet spans edge to edge with 24px padding and keeps its shaped bottom edge; the tear-off strip stacks the email above a full-width button.

sections.name: One field, nothing else
sections.blueprint: The whole section is one prompt and one field in a column 520px wide, on the page's text column line or centred, with 200px of empty ground above and 160px below. The prompt is two lines at one size, 24–28px in medium weight: the first line in the soft ink, the second in full ink. 28px below, a single input 520px wide and 64px tall with a 12px radius, filled with the lightest tone on the page so it is the only bright surface in view; no outline at rest and a 2px inner ring in the accent on focus. Inside the right end of the field, 8px from its edge, a round submit button 44px across with an arrow and an accessible name. 16px below the field, one line at 13px says what happens next. 72px lower, three label and value rows at 14px: email, phone, address.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Prompt at 22px. The field stays one row, 60px tall, with the arrow button inside its right end. The three label and value rows stack with the label above each value and 20px between them.

references.name: Flowjam
references.idea: A persistent frosted sidebar card holds the pitch and buttons while a soft-serif content column scrolls past it; beyond that there is no idea stronger than proof by logos and videos.
references.hero: Grainy off-white page. A tall rounded card about 26% of the viewport wide is pinned at the left and runs off the bottom; frosted over blurred pink and yellow flowers, it holds the logo, a two-line serif tagline, a short blurb and two pill buttons in hot pink and charcoal. The main column starts 32% from the left: a hot-pink pill badge, a three-line serif headline at 4.2vw, then a paragraph whose first sentence is grey and the rest black. A lone charcoal pill button floats far right at mid-height. Below: a heart icon with a proof line, then the top of a four-column logo grid with dotted borders.
references.type: Gelica throughout: a soft, slightly bulbous serif at regular weight, 60px headline with tight -0.05em tracking, 16 to 19px body, down to about 9px in the sidebar. One family for everything including buttons keeps the tone warm but flattens the difference between labels and prose.
references.colour: #f8f8f6 #e7e8e4 #1c0f1f #ff4fe0 #0c0c0c #7b3ff2 — Warm paper white with grain, near-black aubergine text and one hot-pink accent used for the badge and primary button; a purple heart appears once. The footer flips to black.
references.imagery: Rounded-corner video thumbnails of founders talking to camera and product UI clips, each with a small round play button bottom-left; monochrome client logos in a dotted-line grid; blurred floral blobs behind the frosted sidebar.
references.layout: A fixed 26% sidebar card at left for the whole scroll; content occupies one column to its right, split into two for video tiles and four for logos. Sections are separated by whitespace only. The footer is a rounded black panel that still leaves the sidebar in place.

sections.description: Four-column grid of client logos drawn with faint dotted cell borders, each cell roughly 240px wide and 115px tall with the logo centred in dark grey monochrome. Sixteen or more logos over four rows, no captions. Above it, a centred line with a purple heart glyph and a sentence whose first word is black and the rest grey serves as the heading.

Two-column grid of video cards. Each card has a header row with the client name in 14px serif and a one-line result in tiny grey beneath it at left, and a small outlined pill link at right; then a 16:9 thumbnail with about 10px radius and a round play button over its bottom-left corner. Cards are divided by hairlines rather than boxes, and some thumbnails are flat type frames instead of photos.

A rounded black panel inset from the page edges, sitting right of the sidebar. Its background is a short phrase repeated in dark-grey serif at about 5vw, rows offset so the words tile like wallpaper. Centred over it: a two-line white serif headline at about 2.5vw and a small stat line. The lower third holds the logo at left and four narrow columns of tiny text.

steal: Pin a narrow card with logo, one-line pitch and both actions beside the scrolling content, so the call to action never leaves the screen and no top nav is needed.
Set one sentence of a paragraph in grey and the rest in black to rank two claims without changing size or weight.
Tile a short phrase as dark-on-black wallpaper behind the footer headline.

references.name: Rafael Derolez
references.idea: A portfolio as a phone carousel: a fixed text rail on the left narrates whichever phone-shaped screen is centred on the right.
references.hero: Dark charcoal page split by a vertical hairline at 30% width. Left rail: a 55px header row with name, slash and current section as a breadcrumb in 16px sans, plus a small cobalt ticket-shaped hire button with a perforated divider and arrow; below a hairline, four short paragraphs of 16px grey text with white links, top-aligned, leaving the lower 40% of the rail empty. Right 70%: three phone-proportioned frames with large rounded corners in a row; the centre one upright, full brightness and about 680px tall, the outer two smaller, dimmed and rotated in perspective toward the centre.
references.type: Suisse at a single 16px size, weight 400, for everything; hierarchy comes only from grey versus white and from the breadcrumb. The one larger setting is a bold two-word line inside the blue contact card. No display type at all.
references.colour: #18181b #030303 #969696 #173ded #ffffff — Zinc-black field with grey text and white for links and the active breadcrumb. Cobalt blue appears only on the hire button and contact card; all other colour comes from the app screenshots.
references.imagery: Phone-shaped frames with large corner radius holding app screens, a selfie and short videos; side frames are dimmed to about 40% and tilted in 3D like a cover-flow.
references.layout: Single viewport, no page scroll: a fixed 432px text rail with 32px padding and a media stage filling the rest. Scrolling advances the carousel and replaces the rail's text; hairlines separate rail, header and stage. On mobile the stage stacks above the rail.

sections.description: Same two-part frame. The breadcrumb's last word changes to the project name; under the header sit three tiny grey meta tags (employer, platform), then two paragraphs. On the stage the centred phone shows the product screen at full brightness while neighbours show the previous and next items dimmed and tilted, so the carousel works as both navigation and preview.

In the rail, a cobalt card shaped like a ticket with notched sides: tiny labels top-left and top-right, a large bold two-word heading, name and local time in small text, then a perforated lower strip with email at left and a copy button at right. Under it, a career list: company in white with dates in small grey on one line, role on the next, and a small arrow at the far right of each row.

steal: Use a breadcrumb (name / current item) as the only heading and update its last word as the content changes.
Show work in device-shaped frames arranged as a cover-flow, with neighbours dimmed and tilted so the next item is always previewed.
Shape the contact card like a ticket with notches and a perforated strip so the one accent-colour element feels like an object.

references.name: Maria Vasilyeva
references.idea: A designer's work treated as a playlist: every project is a track on one horizontal timeline, the wheel moves a playhead along it, and the track under the playhead blooms out of a thin strip of thumbnails into a scattered collage, with a hand-written layer of margin notes on top that can be switched off like the sound.
references.hero: One fixed 1440x900 off-white stage. Two near-black rails about 26px wide, inset 10px from the left and right edges, carry all the chrome as small vertical caps: name and role on the left reading upward, the menu and on/off toggles for sound and notes on the right. Seven faint lines every 112px divide the field into eight tracks; along the middle one runs a 32px strip of miniature thumbnails across the full width, the whole body of work in sequence, crossed by a thin vertical playhead. Around the playhead the current project's 10-20 images leave the strip and settle into an overlapping collage about 450-770px wide, with a small uppercase serif title and superscript year pinned to its upper-left corner. A hand-written scroll cue sits in a drawn oval at top centre (about 2.5vw), and a bottom row at y=868 gives the project number, name and link. No headline.
references.type: Three families. A high-contrast display serif (63% of characters) for project titles, uppercase at 29px (2vw), -0.02em, leading 1, with the year as a small superscript. A typewriter-style face (31%) for every small label at 13-15px. A loose hand-written script (6%) is the largest type on the page at 36.7px (2.5vw), used only for two notes. The house version drops the typewriter face for the text face and sets the label row in sentence case.
references.colour: #f9f9f9 #131313 #e9e9e9 #626262 — Strictly neutral: off-white ground on about 94% of the screen, near-black for the rails, the loader and text, a pale grey for the track lines, a mid grey for secondary text. Every hue arrives inside the project images: lavender product screens, deep greens, warm wood browns.
references.imagery: Case-study images of products and screens in mixed ratios (16:10 screens, portrait product shots), square corners, no shadows or filters, each keeping its own colour; pieces overlap freely and crop each other. Hand-drawn strokes, an oval round the scroll cue and a curling arrow to the project link, are the only illustration.
references.layout: No document scroll: a single stage whose content changes in place. The working field runs between the rails from x=48 to x=1390; the collage covers 30-50% of the width at a time and moves with the playhead, so 50-70% of the field is blank off-white, closed by the strip and the rails. A bottom row on a 4 | 1fr | 4 column grid. On the phone the rails become black bars at the top and bottom and the collage stacks above and below the strip.

sections.description: The loader: a near-black screen with the same faint tracks, a tiny percentage counter bottom centre, then groups of five short uppercase serif lines of music-themed loading phrases that slide in from the right over about 3.5s, each dragging a trail of its first letter repeated, before a 1.2s curtain reveals the stage.

The strip as the index: a 32px band of 30-60px thumbnails at the vertical centre, every project's images in sequence across the full width, with the playhead marking the current position; the bottom row repeats the same three facts for every project, number left, name centred, link right.

The notes layer: two hand-written notes at about 2.5vw drawn on with stroke-dashoffset, the scroll instruction in an oval at top centre and a note with a curling arrow pointing at the project link, both switchable from the right rail.

steal: Take the whole interface from one metaphor of the subject, here a playlist: a timeline strip, a playhead, a sound toggle and loader wording that all speak it, so nothing on the screen is filler.

Show the entire body of work at once as a thin thumbnail strip (about 3.5% of the height) and open only the current item into a large composition, so the index and the detail share one screen. The site rules the field with seven hairlines; the house version keeps the bands as space and lets the strip carry the structure.

Use a hand-written layer at about 2.5vw, drawn on with stroke-dashoffset, for at most two instructions (where to scroll, where to click), give it an off switch, and count it as one of the page's two faces.
references.media: One fixed WebGL canvas draws every image: a full-width 32px thumbnail strip plus one project's collage around the playhead, about 25-35% of the pixels in all, the rest off-white. No img or video elements; about 60-80 project images in the strip, 10-20 blooming per project.
references.motion: The loader runs past 4.5s: a counter alone for the first second, then serif lines slide in over 3.5s on cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.36,1) and a 1.2s curtain on (0.7,0.15,0.25,1) clears it. Each wheel step slides the playhead and pulls the next project out of the strip into a collage while the last collapses back, round an endless loop of seven; nearly everything else runs on cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), 1.4s for letter-spacing and transforms and 0.4s for fades, with no reduced-motion rule.
